To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“the mobility diversity, defined in terms entropy of individual users’ trajectories and computed from mobile phone data, exhibits significant correlation with two distinct socio-economic development indicators and is the best predictor of these indicators in a set of predictive models”.

(i) the entropy of the trajectories of individual users, extracted from mobile phone call detail records (CDR) data, exhibits a strong correlation with two different measures of well-being, and (ii) it is a good predictor for the same two indicators.

the diversity of individual mobility, defined in the context of mobile phone data as the entropy of individual trajectories, is significantly correlated with two different socio-economical indicators and that it exhibits the highest importance in models built to predict these socio-economical variables.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: Can the diversity of mobility be used to nowcast socio-economic development and human well-being?
the development of a new data-driven analytical framework to estimate and nowcast socio-economic indicators using mobility and social measures derived from mobile phone data.
the following question: can mobile phone data nowcast socio-economic development and wellbeing?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have shown how mobile phone data can be used to estimate and predict socio-economic indicators.

our results suggest that mobility diversity is a promising proxy of well-being, which is consistent with the hypothesis that the more diverse and heterogeneous the mobility of a territory, the more well-being is distributed and shared in that territory.

the entropy of the individual trajectories of mobile phone users, extracted from mobile phone call detail records, exhibits significant correlation with two socio-economic indicators and the highest predictive power in models to nowcast the well-being of a territory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can use mobile phone data to monitor and predict the well-being of a country, and that we can do it with a high degree of confidence.
we have designed a framework to estimate socio-economic indicators using mobility measures derived from mobile phone data.

the entropy of mobility, as a new indicator, can provide a proxy for the socio-economic development and the well-being of a territory, and that this proxy is more informative than other indicators that have been used so far.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in addition to the traditional socio-economic data, mobile phone data can be a valuable source of information for the analysis of socio-economic phenomena.
mobility diversity, which is an information-theoretic measure, can be used as a proxy for socio-economic development.
we can use Big Data to monitor socio-economic development and predict well-being.
